questions.question: Which system includes bones and provides structural support?
choices: Digestive
Endocrine
Urinary
Skeletal

questions.question: Which system includes muscles that move the skeleton?
choices: Respiratory
Muscular
Lymphatic
Integumentary

questions.question: Which organ is a major part of the integumentary system?
choices: Stomach
Kidney
Skin
Pancreas

questions.question: What is the main role of the digestive system?
choices: Break down food and absorb nutrients
Move nutrients through vessels without breaking down food
Regulate movement mainly through electrical signaling
Filter waste from blood and regulate salt balance

questions.question: Which organs filter blood and help regulate water and salts?
choices: Kidneys
Lungs
Small intestines
Salivary glands

questions.question: What is a tissue?
choices: Several organs coordinating a body function
An individual cell's internal membrane network
A group of cells and associated material performing related functions
All organisms of one species in an area

questions.question: What is an organ?
choices: A single specialized cell performing all body functions
A structure composed of multiple tissues working together
A group of similar cells without multiple tissue types
Several body systems grouped as one structure

questions.question: Why do body systems function together rather than independently?
choices: Each system supplies every resource it requires by itself
Transport systems can work without regulation from other systems
Cooperation is required only during illness
Cells need coordinated transport, regulation, and resource supply

questions.question: How do the digestive and circulatory systems interact?
choices: Food travels intact through arteries to each body cell
Absorbed nutrients remain in the digestive tract
Absorbed nutrients enter transport pathways supplying tissues
Blood vessels release most digestive enzymes into the stomach

questions.question: How do muscles and bones cooperate in movement?
choices: Muscle contractions pull on bones through attachments
Bones contract while muscles remain rigid
Muscles push bones without attachments
Bones move without forces

questions.question: Why is the small intestine's large internal surface useful?
choices: It increases the volume available for storing undigested food
It filters blood in place of the kidneys
It transfers oxygen directly from inhaled air
It supports efficient nutrient absorption

questions.question: How does skin contribute to maintaining internal conditions?
choices: It controls body temperature mainly by filtering blood
It provides a barrier and participates in temperature regulation
It supplies most absorbed nutrients to body cells
It produces the body's digestive enzymes

questions.question: Why must the urinary system regulate water and dissolved salts?
choices: Body fluids should contain no salts
Cell function depends on suitable internal concentrations
Water balance affects only the urinary organs
Any internal salt concentration supports equal cell function

questions.question: What does negative feedback do in many body-control systems?
choices: Amplifies every departure indefinitely
Prevents detection of changes
Keeps every quantity exactly constant
Counteracts a departure from a suitable range

questions.question: How does the lymphatic system help body fluid balance?
choices: It returns excess tissue fluid to circulation
It removes water from the body through the lungs
It produces the main enzymes used in digestion
It transports impulses from skin receptors to the brain

questions.question: A student arranges cells, tissues, organs, and systems. Which order goes from simpler to more complex?
choices: Organs → cells → systems → tissues
Systems → tissues → cells → organs
Cells → tissues → organs → systems
Tissues → organs → cells → systems

questions.question: A muscle contracts but its tendon cannot transmit force normally. Which function is directly affected?
choices: Absorbing food in the intestine
Filtering blood in a kidney
Producing skin pigment
Moving the attached bone

questions.question: After nutrients are absorbed, how can they reach cells far from the digestive tract?
choices: Movement mainly through sensory neurons
Direct diffusion across the entire body without transport
Transport by circulation
Passage only through the interiors of bones

questions.question: A model includes protection, sensation, and sweat release. Which system does it chiefly represent?
choices: Integumentary
Digestive
Skeletal
Reproductive

questions.question: An organ has epithelial, connective, muscular, and nervous tissues. What does this demonstrate?
choices: Each tissue functions as a separate complete organ
An organ can combine several tissue types
An organ always contains only one cell type
Tissue type determines an organ's entire role independently
